clue.text: Calorie consumed in diet — see Scottish scale

indicators.note: something consumed in a thing ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to diet is to slim
C is the standard abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: A dieter counting calories is told to check the Scottish bathroom scales.
explanation.walkthrough: SCLIM is a Scots word meaning to climb, and 'scale' here is the verb, not the weighing machine the dieting surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall is to climb it, and sclim is the Scots dialect verb for climbing.

clue.text: More experienced students appeal for help about high pressure rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
about means going around, so the distress call surrounds the other piece

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
HP is the standard abbreviation for high pressure

explanation.surface: Senior students call for help as the pressure on them mounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophs is American college slang for sophomores, second-year students, who have more experience than freshmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophomores are second-year students in the US, so they are more experienced than first-years.

clue.text: Lieutenant not appearing in fashionable armour

indicators.note: not appearing in a word means being left out of it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a cult film or band is fashionable among its followers
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: An army officer is absent from the parade of fashionable armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuish (or cuisse) is a piece of plate armour protecting the thigh.

clue.text: This darn law waves — will thanadar perhaps?

definitions.text: This darn law waves — will thanadar perhaps?

indicators.note: something that waves moves to and fro, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are in the anagram along with the answer

explanation.surface: An Indian police officer is expected to brandish this to enforce a dreadful law.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: this answer plus the letters of 'darn law', jumbled, give 'will thanadar'. A thanadar is an Indian police station chief, and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick bound with iron, carried by Indian police, which an officer would wave at a crowd.

clue.text: For local turning up I measure round — it'll ease the pain

indicators.note: round means placed on both sides of, so the outer pieces enclose the rest

parts.note: taken as written
an en is a printer's measure of width

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means read from the bottom, so the order is backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the local is your nearest pub

explanation.surface: Someone heads up to the local pub and measures a round of drinks to ease their pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For local' read backwards is the core, with I in front and the printer's measure behind. In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common over-the-counter painkiller, an anti-inflammatory drug taken to relieve aches.

clue.text: Cooper's requirement? Beer of reduced scope (12, two words)

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the short word loses its last letter

parts.note: bitter is a British style of draught beer
taken as written, then shortened
the scope of a study is its range

explanation.surface: A barrel-maker needs beer, though apparently only a modest amount.
explanation.walkthrough: A cooper makes barrels, but Frank Cooper's is a famous Oxford marmalade brand, made from bitter Seville oranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade such as Cooper's is made from Seville oranges, so the bitter fruit is the maker's essential ingredient.

clue.text: New US cemetery mostly in sun? Help for metalworker

indicators.note: in puts the preceding pieces inside the word for the sun

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia is the US military burial ground

explanation.surface: A new American cemetery basks in the sunshine, oddly linked to a metalworker.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarling tool is a long-armed iron used by metalworkers to raise embossed work from inside a hollow vessel.

clue.text: Tenant-farmer having to fret, say in recession

indicators.note: a thing in recession moves backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: to fret is to wear away by rubbing
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'

explanation.surface: A tenant-farmer, worried by a recession, is driven to fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: A gebur was a tenant-farmer in Anglo-Saxon England; the economic 'recession' of the surface is just a turning-back signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives gebur as the Old English word for a tenant farmer holding land from a lord.

clue.text: One who often worked with Renoir in choosing a binder

definitions.text: One who often worked with Renoir

indicators.note: in says the name sits inside the words that follow, spanning their gap

parts.note: the letters run across three words

explanation.surface: A painter's assistant helping Renoir pick a binding medium for his paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Renoir suggests the painter Auguste, but here it is his son, the film director Jean Renoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Gabin starred in Jean Renoir's films, including La Grande Illusion and La Bête humaine, so he was a frequent collaborator.

clue.text: E. Indian tree: one branch forming something for switch-hitter to grasp

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold inside the hand, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a switch-hitter is a bisexual, slang 'bi'
I is the Roman numeral one
a limb is a large branch of a tree

explanation.surface: A baseball player who bats either way grips a branch of an Indian tree as a bat.
explanation.walkthrough: A switch-hitter bats both left and right in baseball, which is also slang for a bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: The bilimbi is a small tree of the East Indies related to the carambola, grown for its sour fruit.

clue.text: Like complete deck made of one wood, tons

parts.note: 'un is dialect for one, as in 'a good 'un'
deal is pine or fir timber
t is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A ship's deck built entirely of one kind of timber, weighing tons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' suggests a ship's planking, which suits the wood; it is a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A full pack of cards before the deal is undealt, still complete in the dealer's hand.

clue.text: Trendy young Aussie guy's time to swagger

parts.note: a Roy is Australian slang for a trendy young man; the possessive adds the s
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A fashionable young Australian man takes his moment to strut about.
explanation.definitionFit: Royst is an old variant of roist, to bluster or swagger noisily.

clue.text: Dark blue camel's hair coat, fashionable? It's poisonous

parts.note: the Dark Blues are Oxford University, whose colour is dark blue
an aba is an Arab cloak woven from camel's or goat's hair
in, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A query about whether a navy camel-hair coat is in fashion, ending in an alarming warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's sporting colour is dark blue, Cambridge's light blue, so 'Dark blue' stands for Oxford University. Ouabain is an arrow poison from African plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouabain is a toxic glycoside used by African hunters as an arrow poison, so it is a substance that is poisonous.

clue.text: Descriptive of an acid accounting for a raincoat

parts.note: taken as written
a mino is a Japanese raincoat made of straw or rushes

explanation.surface: A chemistry note claiming some acid is what makes a raincoat waterproof.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is the adjective in 'amino acid', so the definition is an adjective describing a class of acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino is the qualifier in amino acid, naming acids that contain the NH2 group, the building blocks of protein.

clue.text: Mucus troubled Patti accepting central part in Louise

indicators.note: letters that are troubled are disturbed and thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the central part of a name is its middle, so only those letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the six-letter name

explanation.surface: Patti, troubled by mucus, takes in a friend called Louise.
explanation.definitionFit: Pituita is an old medical term for phlegm, the thick secretion the body produces.

clue.text: Jock's prison crop concealed by herbal dyes

indicators.note: something concealed by words sits out of sight within them, running across the gap

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A Scottish prisoner's haircut is hidden under herbal dyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is crossword shorthand for a Scot; a baldy is Scots for a crew cut, the very short haircut associated with prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists baldy as a Scots term for a close-cropped haircut, the style given to inmates.

clue.text: Exercise if inside is irritating or is appalling

parts.note: physical education, the school exercise lesson

indicators.note: inside places a short word within the longer one that follows it

parts.note: as in 'he tries my patience'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that exercise is irritating at best and dreadful at worst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' links the two halves: the first half builds the word, the second gives its meaning as a verb phrase in the third person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that petrifies you appals you, freezing you with horror, so 'is appalling' matches the third-person verb.

clue.text: With which one looks forward to Sat. and old-style bonhomie?

definitions.text: With which one looks forward to Sat.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Shakespeare's word for friendliness

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: split the answer as Fri. ending, the close of Friday, which leads straight into Saturday.
explanation.definitionFit: Friending is a Shakespearean noun for friendliness or goodwill, an archaic word for warm sociability.

clue.text: This recipe is flexible — it can be stuffed or boiled!

definitions.text: it can be stuffed or boiled!

indicators.note: something flexible bends into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin 'take') on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cookery tip: this recipe adapts to stuffing or boiling, like a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The food picture is the trap: a stuffed shirt is a pompous person, and a boiled shirt is a starched dress shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed shirt and boiled shirt are both fixed phrases, so a shirt is the garment that can be described either way.

clue.text: Hopeless as member of cast for endless soap, awful bilge

parts.note: an actor who is a member of the cast is in it

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are jumbled
without an end, the final letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Corrie is the nickname of Coronation Street, Britain's longest-running TV soap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic says an actor is hopeless for joining the cast of a long-running soap full of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Coronation Street is a British TV soap opera, known as Corrie.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incorrigible cannot be reformed, so the case is hopeless; the adjectives are near synonyms.

clue.text: Flower (delicate?) is raised in place renowned for games once

indicators.note: in places the short word within the name of the place

parts.note: Nemea in Greece hosted the ancient Nemean Games

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means lifted from bottom to top, so the short word is reversed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A query whether a delicate flower is grown at an ancient sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympia is the obvious games site, but the letters need Nemea, home of another of the four ancient Greek games.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesia is a South African garden plant with bright, delicate-looking flowers grown as an annual bedding plant.

clue.text: Scholars no longer knock off round master, uplifted

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: cly is old thieves' cant for steal, no longer in use

indicators.note: in a down entry, uplifted means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: sire is an old form of address to a lord or master

explanation.surface: Scholars of old would bring down a master, then raise him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' looks part of the definition but marks the steal word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: The clerisy is the learned class, scholars and intellectuals considered as a body.

clue.text: Examples of vanity shown by mischievous child caught formerly in poses

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces within the word for poses

parts.note: a model sits or poses for an artist
a little elf is a mischievous child
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
once means at a former time

explanation.surface: A spoilt child, photographed once too often, shows off vanity in every pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-conceit is an inflated opinion of oneself, so instances of it are examples of vanity.

clue.text: It's soft inside straw once bound round

indicators.note: inside places the soft letter within the word for a straw

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount, like a straw in 'not worth a straw'
p is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Something soft lies within a bundle of straw tied round.
explanation.walkthrough: Whipt is the archaic spelling of whipped, and to whip a rope is to bind it round with twine.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip is to bind tightly with cord, so whipt is the old past participle for bound round.

clue.text: Conifers cop cut from thicket, absent

indicators.note: cut from means removed out of, so a word is taken off the front of the longer one

parts.note: taken as written
a coppice is a thicket of small trees
a is the register abbreviation for absent

explanation.surface: A policeman cuts through a thicket of conifers but is nowhere to be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Picea is the botanical genus of spruces, a group of evergreen cone-bearing trees.

clue.text: Over beloved, losing inner attention

indicators.note: losing an inner part means letters are taken from the middle of the word

parts.note: someone endeared to you is beloved
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A lover's attention fades once the affair is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' at the front looks like a preposition but is the definition, meaning finished.
explanation.definitionFit: When a match is over it has ended, so the past participle stands for finished.

clue.text: Specific type of compound, obscure on turning up

parts.note: a dim light is obscure

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top, so the short word runs backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: A chemist describes an obscure compound coming to light.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimer is a molecule formed by two identical units joined, a particular kind of chemical compound.

clue.text: One of our classically fair girls, in short, scored irregularly

indicators.note: in short means abbreviated, so a word is cut to its initial

parts.words: One of our classically fair girls
parts.note: an English rose is a fair-skinned English girl

explanation.surface: A traditional English beauty whose exam marks were patchy.
explanation.walkthrough: An English rose is the stereotype of a fair-skinned, pretty English girl; 'in short' cuts the first word to its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Erose is a botanical term for a leaf edge that is unevenly notched, as if gnawed or irregularly scored.

clue.text: Primer finished, put on first of topcoat

parts.note: a finished job is done

indicators.note: first of points at the opening letter of the following word only

parts.note: the first letter of topcoat

explanation.surface: A decorator's note: once the primer is done, the topcoat goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is painting; the answer is a school book, named after the Latin grammarian Donatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A donet is an archaic word for a grammar or elementary textbook, an introductory primer.

clue.text: Needing surgical repair, botched in re death

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so the letters that follow come out in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal memo about a death after a botched operation that needed surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in re' is legal Latin for 'in the matter of', making the surface read like a case file.
explanation.definitionFit: A herniated disc or gut has ruptured through its wall, a condition usually fixed by surgery.

clue.text: 'Devoted to a goddess' appears as first clue often?

parts.note: to be, as in 'he is a doctor'
1 Ac., one across, is usually the first clue in a crossword

explanation.surface: A puzzle phrase that turns up often as the opening clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'first clue often' as the written form 1 Ac., one across, where the digit 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isiac describes the cult of Isis, the Egyptian goddess, so it means devoted to her worship.

clue.text: On which Mikado was borne, 12 holding edge?

indicators.note: holding means grasping something within, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday
the rim is the edge of a cup or wheel

explanation.surface: A query about the vehicle carrying the Mikado, and how it had a raised rim.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a reference to clue 12 across but is the time, twelve o'clock. The Mikado was the emperor of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A norimon is a Japanese palanquin, a covered litter carried on poles, which bore dignitaries such as the emperor.

clue.text: I step off the beaten track

indicators.note: off means not right, wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wanderer declares they like walking away from the usual paths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the beaten track' is a set phrase, but 'off' splits from it to work alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a ski run of compacted snow, literally a beaten track.

clue.text: Some Indians seen excitedly trailing gazelle

parts.note: the goa is a Tibetan gazelle

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of Indians are spotted excitedly following a gazelle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailing' puts the scrambled letters after the gazelle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goanese are the people of Goa on India's west coast, so they are some of the Indian population.

clue.text: Carnivore (large of its kind) unknown in bracken

indicators.note: in puts the unknown letter inside the word for bracken

parts.note: tara is a New Zealand bracken fern
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

explanation.definitionFit: The tayra is a South American member of the weasel family, unusually big for that family, hence large of its kind.

clue.text: Meet with centre forward presenting feathery plume?

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is moved forward to the front

parts.note: to meet someone is to greet them

explanation.walkthrough: 'centre forward' sounds like a footballer, but it says to move the middle letter forward.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron, and also the term for a tuft of its plumes, or any feathery plume such as on a seed.
